Message:
docs: add staging environment design and implementation plan

Staging runs as a second Compose project on the production VPS: own Postgres,
Redis and MinIO, container names namespaced aivastra-staging-*, host ports at
prod+100. The dev branch deploys to it via the existing ci.yml, with the target
resolved from github.ref.

Data is an unscrubbed prod snapshot refreshed by an operator-run script, so the
.env.staging credentials are the isolation boundary; a pre-deploy guardrail
aborts the deploy when they resemble production's, and a distinct
SHOPIFY_TOKEN_ENC_KEY makes copied merchant tokens undecryptable in staging.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: adeshboudh
Message:
fix(shopify): register mandatory GDPR compliance webhooks

shopify.app.toml had no [webhooks.privacy_compliance] block, so
Shopify's app review flagged missing mandatory customer-privacy
webhooks. The handlers already exist (webhook.routes.ts serves
customers_data_request, customers_redact, shop_redact) — per-shop
registration for them 404s on Shopify's webhooks.json API, so they
must instead be declared once here and take effect on the next
`shopify app deploy`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: adeshboudh
Message:
feat(dev-api): catalog generation from admin-curated assets

The public developer API could only do /v1/dev/tryon, where the caller
supplies both the person and garment images. None of our admin-curated
faces, poses, backgrounds, lower garments or shoes were reachable, so the
one thing that differentiates us from FASHN/fal was invisible to
integrators. Adds three routes, which appear in /v1/dev/openapi.json
automatically by virtue of their zod schemas:

  GET  /v1/dev/catalog/options   asset discovery, ETag + 304
  POST /v1/dev/catalog/generate  garment + slugs -> N jobs, 1 catalogueId
  GET  /v1/dev/catalogues/:id    batch status for all N in one query

Assets are addressed by public slug, never internal UUID: a slug survives
an admin deleting and recreating a row, and integrators hard-code these
values for months. Migration 0130 adds a nullable public_api_slug to the
five asset tables with a partial unique index. That single column carries
both the curation flag and the public name -- NULL means unpublished --
so an exposed-but-unnamed or named-but-hidden drift is impossible. No
backfill; every asset starts unexposed and an admin opts each one in.

Discovery was 8-9 sequential queries returning byte-identical results for
every caller, against a pool of max: 10 per process, so it is now cached
in Redis. Invalidation is a version counter (INCR), not key deletion, so
one bump orphans every cached variant without SCAN or enumeration; the
1h TTL reclaims the orphans. Any Redis failure falls through to a direct
build, so a cache outage costs throughput and never availability. The
generation doubles as the ETag. Keys are namespaced by a hash of
DATABASE_URL because the test harness shares one Redis DB across files
that each own a separate Postgres -- the same hazard applies to any two
deployments sharing a Redis.

Invalidation is one onResponse hook rather than a call in each of the 28
mutating routes in admin/models.routes.ts alone, because per-route bumps
guarantee route #29 ships without one. Audited every writer of the five
tables: the only non-admin path is /v1/backgrounds/mine/:id, which writes
scope: 'user' rows the builder already filters out.

createJob hardcoded source: 'catalog' and never set apiKeyId, so every
job created here would have 404'd on its own status endpoint -- both
/v1/dev/jobs/:id and the new batch route filter source = 'api' and join
api_keys on jobs.apiKeyId. Both are now optional opts defaulting to the
previous behaviour, so no existing caller changes.

The Shopify options query body moves into a shared buildCatalogOptions()
so the pose_garment_configs overlay has exactly one implementation. This
does put the Shopify options route behind the same cache -- intended, it
refetches on every gender/garment-type change today -- but a broken
invalidation hook would now surface there too, so it is covered by a test
and wants a manual pass on that page before merge.

Verified live against local infra with a real API key, not only the
harness: credits deduct and refund transactionally, BAD_SLUG rejects
before any credit or R2 write, and a generated job resolves through
/v1/dev/jobs/:id. 302 tests pass across 39 files (13 new); lint clean;
api/admin-web/types/db build and typecheck clean.

Deferred by design: a dispatcher-written Redis job-status mirror and a
completion webhook. The batch status route is the cheap ~12x cut on
polling; the other two are only worth building once traffic justifies it.

fix(tryon-widget): equalize popup frame size, drop history "View Product"

Modal content was a variable height per step (upload/progress/error
shorter than ready/result), so the popup visibly resized switching
steps. Fix modal height to the ready-step (frame 3) size and make
pages/steps flex-fill it, centering shorter content and scrolling
the history list internally instead of stretching the frame.

Also drop the redundant "View Product" link from history cards —
tapping the thumbnail already opens the result, and the product link
duplicates the merchant's own product page nav.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: adeshboudh
Message:
feat(api): add merchant API key management routes

GET/POST /v1/merchant/api-keys and DELETE /v1/merchant/api-keys/:id,
authed exclusively by the merchant session JWT (requireMerchant) so a
leaked API key can never mint, list, or revoke keys. Plaintext key is
returned only from POST and is never persisted or re-listable.

Two Fastify-specific fixes were needed beyond the plan's literal route
code for the given test to actually pass:
- Fastify 5 runs schema validation before preHandler, so a bodyless
  unauthenticated POST would 400 on body validation before
  requireMerchant got a chance to 401 it. Body shape is now checked
  manually inside the handler (after preHandler) instead of via the
  route's declarative `schema.body`.
- Fastify's default JSON parser throws FST_ERR_CTP_EMPTY_JSON_BODY for
  a bodyless DELETE sent with a content-type: application/json header
  (as raw fetch-based tests do). Added a content-type parser scoped to
  this plugin's own encapsulation context that treats an empty body as
  absent rather than an error.

fix(dispatcher): don't orphan job when terminal refund conflicts

terminateJob() returned early inside the transaction when the
JOB_FAIL_REFUND ledger insert hit its unique (job_id, reason) conflict,
skipping the status=FAILED update along with the balance update. A job

again gets stuck in GENERATING with no code left to touch it, until the
15-minute sweeper force-fails it as STUCK_IN_FLIGHT. Now the balance
update alone is skipped on conflict; the status transition always runs.

Author: srinivasgunnam-nicedigitals
Message:
fix(admin): persist look shot-type tag and stop template poses leaking into custom-pose config

Two bugs found while using the admin templates page after the shot-type
default workflows feature shipped:

- Changing a look's shot-type selector for an already-uploaded pose
  silently discarded the change. PUT .../looks never sent shotType and
  the route didn't accept it - persistence only ever worked via a fresh
  pose (re-)upload. Now the route updates model_pose_assets.shot_type
  for any look carrying one, inside the same transaction, before the
  existing resolveForTemplate cascade.

- "3. Custom look poses" (standalone poses for Create your own look)
  was also showing scope='template' poses uploaded via the catalogue-
  template look builder, because GET .../pose-configs filtered by
  gender only. Added the scope='general' filter - template poses are
  managed only in "2. Catalogue templates" and don't use the
  pose_garment_configs table this panel writes to anyway.

Both verified with a failing-then-passing integration test each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
